figure.name: Elon Musk
figure.era: Platform, space, electric vehicle, and billionaire politics (2000-present)
figure.role: Businessman associated with Tesla, SpaceX, X, xAI, immense paper wealth, public contracts, and direct control of communication platforms.
figure.hook: Musk = founder control, state contracts, platform power, and billionaire politics.
whyHere: Musk belongs here because twenty-first-century capitalism mixes founder mythology, stock-market wealth, state contracts, industrial risk, social media power, and political influence.
He matters because he shows that capitalist power can be private, public-facing, state-supported, and media-shaping at the same time.
figure.cleanIdea: Modern capitalist power can come from owning valuable firms, controlling platforms, winning public contracts, and turning personal reputation into market power. Musk is useful because he forces the page to hold several truths at once: private risk, public subsidy, engineering ambition, securities conflict, labor conflict, and platform control.

hallCard.timelineMeaning: Tesla, SpaceX, X, stock wealth, state contracts, and platform ownership show capitalist power moving through firms, government, markets, and media.

ideas.title: Founder Control
ideas.plainDefinition: Founder control is the power a founder keeps through ownership stakes, voting rights, board influence, brand identity, and investor confidence.
ideas.context: In the Musk path, founder control means the person and the company become hard to separate in markets, media, and politics.
ideas.whyMatters: Founder control matters because capitalism can concentrate authority inside a public company even when many people technically own shares. The founder can become the product, the market signal, the political actor, and the crisis risk all at once.

sources.title: Forbes / Elon Musk profile
sources.note: Source lead for company and wealth framing; supports the branch from personal control to public-company market power.

ideas.title: State Contracts
ideas.plainDefinition: State contracts are public contracts awarded to private firms for services, infrastructure, technology, military, space, health, or other public purposes.
ideas.context: In the Musk path, SpaceX shows that private capitalism and public funding can be deeply intertwined.
ideas.whyMatters: State contracts matter because a company can be private and still depend on public missions, public money, and public risk. This is where the simple slogan 'government versus business' breaks down: capitalist firms can build public projects with public contracts while keeping private ownership.

ideas.title: Attention Platform
ideas.plainDefinition: An attention platform is a privately controlled media or social platform that shapes what people see, share, monetize, fight over, or believe is visible.
ideas.context: In the Musk path, Twitter/X turns ownership into direct influence over a public communication arena.
ideas.whyMatters: Attention platforms matter because speech, politics, advertising, identity, and markets now move through privately owned infrastructure. Owning the platform is not the same as owning every opinion on it, but it can shape moderation, visibility, monetization, and public conflict.
